title: 3D-printed zirconia partial crowns: A clinical prospective single-arm pilot study
summary:
There has recently been the possibility to fabricate ceramic dental restorations using 3D printing, a variant of additive manufacturing (AM). Despite the potential of 3D printing for dentistry and the availability of a clinically approved 3D printer and corresponding materials, there are still only few studies on the clinical longevity of 3D-printed zirconia partial crowns. The aim of this study is therefore to investigate the longevity and clinical quality of 3D-printed zirconia partial crowns. The primary endpoint is the survival probability of the restorations, while secondary endpoints include compliance with the FDI criteria (e.g., marginal adaptation, surface quality) and the clinical accuracy of fit during placement.
In in-vitro tests, the fit accuracy (marginal and internal fit) of 3D-printed zirconia partial crowns will first be evaluated on 10 standardized plastic teeth with norm preparations. The clinical phase will include 20 legally competent adult patients with the indication for a partial crown restoration in the posterior region. The 3D-printed restorations will be fabricated from high-strength zirconia (INNI-CERA BCM 1000, Aon, Seoul, Korea) using the ZIPRO-D printer (also Aon) and placed clinically. After insertion, follow-up examinations are planned after one week (baseline evaluation) as well as after 6 months, 1 year, 2 years, 3 years, and 5 years. These examinations will include the assessment of clinical parameters and FDI criteria, as well as photographic documentation, in addition to routine dental check-ups.
conditions: partial loss of dental hard tissue

interventions.name: 3D-printed zirconia partial crowns placed in the posterior region

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients’ capacity to give informed consent
- Permanent molar requiring restoration due to caries or trauma, with the indication for a partial crown covering all cusps
- Vitality: vital tooth or endodontically treated tooth with an adequate root canal treatment extending to the apical third and with no evidence of periapical inflammation
- Presence of an antagonistic tooth
- No untreated periodontal disease
- Patient is capable of performing normal daily oral hygiene
- Sufficient knowledge of the German language
Exclusion criteria:
- Parafunction or bruxism
- Poor prognosis: the tooth is unlikely to remain in the mouth for the next 5 years
- Physical limitations or disabilities that prevent normal oral hygiene
- Pulp-preserving measures required (direct or indirect pulp capping, partial pulpotomy)
- Signs of severely neglected oral hygiene
- Pregnancy or breastfeeding
- Disease requiring antibiotic prophylaxis prior to dental treatment
